channel.title: Blocktape
channel.description: Blocktape reports crypto news: exchange and market moves, protocol upgrades, token launches, security incidents, regulation and enforcement across chains.

item.title: Bridge transfers need gas on both sides of the transaction
item.description: A bridge transfer can require gas on both networks: estimate the source transaction, keep native tokens for later steps, and verify what the quote includes.

item.title: Manta Pacific Withdrawals Still Depend on Ethereum Finality
item.description: Manta Pacific withdrawals settle through an Ethereum proof, a challenge window and a final transaction; Manta’s fast-finality plan changes the wait after rollout.

item.title: Cross-chain deposit channels can preserve access after vault changes
item.description: Cross-chain deposit channels can outlive vault changes, but their time limits still matter; learn how address reuse, key handovers and expiry affect late funds.

item.title: Treasury should reconcile Chainflip swaps from deposit to payout
item.description: Treasury should match each Chainflip source deposit to its destination payout, record fees and execution value separately, and keep failed or partial swaps open.

item.title: Cross-chain swap payouts depend on price, liquidity and fees
item.description: Your cross-chain swap payout depends on the route price, pool depth, protocol fees and destination gas; compare the final quoted amount, not the headline rate.

item.title: Chainflip swaps: when Standard, Boost or DCA fits
item.description: Standard executes a swap in one pass, Boost pays to shorten deposit confirmation, and DCA divides execution over time; choose by urgency, size and price risk.

item.title: Three Slippage Choices for Your First Solana Swap
item.description: A Solana swap’s slippage setting limits how far execution may move from the quote; choose tight, balanced or wide based on liquidity, volatility and urgency.

item.title: Why a Solana swap stays pending or fails
item.description: A pending Solana swap may still be waiting for confirmation; a failed one has an execution error. Check its status, blockhash, fee balance and slippage before retrying.

item.title: Crypto treasuries match cross-chain transfers to usable balances
item.description: Cross-chain treasury reconciliation matches source debits to destination credits, fees and pending transfers so finance teams can report usable balances at each close.

item.title: Bridge Quotes Show a Route’s Terms, Not a Guaranteed Arrival
item.description: A bridge quote is an estimate until its minimum output, fees, route steps and expiry are clear; check the transaction’s final terms before approving it.

item.title: How DEX Integrators Should Read Liquidity Lock Periods
item.description: Liquidity locks restrict when LP positions can be withdrawn, but they do not freeze pool reserves; integrators should measure available depth and expiry risk.

item.title: Why an Avalanche Swap Is Pending or Fails
item.description: Avalanche swaps can stall because a C-Chain transaction is queued, underfunded or rejected by the swap contract; check its status before resubmitting.

item.title: Blackhole swap routes: AVAX-to-token or token-to-token?
item.description: AVAX-to-token and token-to-token swaps differ in the asset you start with, the AVAX you need for network costs and how you judge the quoted output.

item.title: LP Tokens Change the Claim, Not the Pool
item.description: LP tokens turn a pool deposit into a transferable claim; moving them changes who can redeem the share while pool balances, fees and price exposure keep moving.

item.title: AMM reserves determine the price of your next swap
item.description: An AMM quotes from the tokens in its pool: trade size, fees and available liquidity determine how far your execution price moves from the displayed spot price.

item.title: Treasury swap slippage budgets set the execution limit
item.description: A treasury slippage budget sets the worst acceptable swap output before execution, balancing price movement, route costs and failed transactions without hiding fees.

item.title: Estimate transferFrom Energy from the call, not a flat rate
item.description: A transferFrom estimate depends on contract execution, account state and the caller’s available resources; simulate the exact call before setting a fee limit.

item.title: How to Reduce Hashing Energy in TRON Contract Calls
item.description: Hashing costs on TRON depend on input size and repetition; profile calls, trim redundant work and set a measured Energy limit without weakening checks.

item.title: Why a first USDT transfer costs more energy on TRON
item.description: A first USDT transfer can use more TRON Energy because it creates the recipient’s balance record; the sender pays for that contract work in network resources or TRX.

item.title: Why Your Crypto Swap Is Still Pending
item.description: A swap can remain pending because its source transaction is unconfirmed, its route is waiting on another network, or the provider has not settled the trade yet.
